clue.text: With support he crosses a public thoroughfare very fast

parts.note: a post is an upright that supports something

indicators.note: the word he is laid across the street, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street, a public thoroughfare

explanation.surface: Someone with a walking aid hurries over a busy road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crosses' makes HE straddle the street; 'public thoroughfare' is the full form behind the abbreviation for street.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an old adverb for with all possible speed, from letters sent by post-horse.

clue.text: Nut-tree growing in Cape Canaveral

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words Cape Canaveral, read across the gap

explanation.surface: A tree is sprouting at the Florida space centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing' is a link; 'in' signals letters lying in Cape Canaveral: caPE CANaveral.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is a North American hickory tree grown for its nuts.

clue.text: During quiet drink, doctor is seen to walk awkwardly

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet

indicators.note: the doctor comes during the drink, so his letters go inside it

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor is seen staggering after a quiet drink.
explanation.walkthrough: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is the usual crossword doctor; 'During' says he sits inside the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To shamble is to move with a clumsy, shuffling gait.

clue.text: Eager and intent to identify an African

parts.note: hot means eager, keen
read 'intent' as IN TENT: the word to goes inside TENT, giving TENTOT

explanation.surface: Someone keen and determined to pin down a person's African origins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intent' is split as 'in tent', so TO sits in TENT. HOTTENTOT is an old, now offensive name for the Khoikhoi people of southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The term was a colonial name for a member of the Khoikhoi people of South Africa.

clue.text: Skating figure in which one is bound to be beaten

definitions.meaning: a move on ice with the body stretched out

definitions.text: in which one is bound to be beaten
definitions.meaning: a position for corporal punishment, tied with limbs outspread

explanation.surface: A figure on ice that sounds like a flogging position.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread eagle is a skating figure with arms and legs outstretched, and a punishment where a person is tied limbs outstretched for flogging.

clue.text: Decline to become Mrs Browning initially

indicators.note: the starting letter of each part of the poet's full name is taken

parts.note: the Victorian poet Elizabeth Barrett Browning, wife of Robert Browning
the Victorian poet Elizabeth Barrett Browning, wife of Robert Browning
the Victorian poet Elizabeth Barrett Browning, wife of Robert Browning

explanation.surface: Refusing to turn into a Victorian poet's wife at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' is a link; 'initially' picks the first letters of Mrs Browning's full name, which the clue does not print.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede or fall away, as the tide does when it goes out.

clue.text: Firm paid for traveller always on the move

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
to meet a bill is to pay it, so met means paid

explanation.surface: A company covered the costs of someone constantly travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet travels endlessly on its orbit through space.

clue.text: Singers producing sheets for listeners?

indicators.note: to those hearing it, the word for sheets is said aloud and gives a sound-alike

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Singers handing out song sheets to the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: QUIRE and CHOIR are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is a group of singers performing together.

clue.text: Male worker takes the blame for setting a snare

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's stock worker insect
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: A man at work takes the fall for laying a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantrap is a trap set to catch trespassers, a kind of snare.

clue.text: Valuer in charge of funds

definitions.meaning: one who prizes things, read as one who treasures
the official who manages a club's or company's money

explanation.surface: An assessor who also looks after the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whimsically, one who treasures something is a valuer; and a treasurer is the officer managing an organisation's money.

clue.text: Honour more fitting for a religious body

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
apter is more apt, more fitting

explanation.surface: A distinction more suitable for a church group.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapter is the body of canons of a cathedral or members of a religious order.

clue.text: Short guide for making a nutty cake

definitions.meaning: a young, small member of the Guides movement
a dense chocolate square, often with walnuts

explanation.surface: A guidebook in brief for baking a nut cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short guide' plays on height: Brownies are the youngest Guides.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brownie is a junior member of the Girl Guides, and a brownie is a chocolate cake often made with nuts.

clue.text: Half-heartedly steal an old gold coin

indicators.note: half of the doubled letter at the heart of the word for steal is dropped

parts.note: to nobble is to steal, in British slang

explanation.surface: Feebly trying to pinch an antique sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: NOBBLE's heart is BB; 'Half-heartedly' loses one B.
explanation.definitionFit: The noble was an English gold coin first struck under Edward III.

clue.text: Bream thrown out by Greek is floating in the sea

indicators.note: the fish's letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish tossed back into the sea by a Greek fisherman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' rearranges BREAM into AMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy substance from sperm whales, often found drifting on the ocean.

clue.text: Very little money invested in Scottish mountain railway to hold a celebration

indicators.note: the money is put into the mountain, its letters inside

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis
one cent, I CENT, is very little money
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pennies poured into a Highland mountain railway to mark an anniversary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very little money' reads as one cent, written I CENT. BEN as in Ben Nevis is a Scottish mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicentenary is a two-hundredth anniversary, an occasion for celebrating.

clue.text: Maiden leaves dwelling to do a spot of gardening

definitions.text: to do a spot of gardening

indicators.note: the maiden departs, so her letter is taken away

parts.note: a home is a dwelling
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman leaves the house to do some weeding.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoe is to break up soil or weed with a long-handled tool.

clue.text: Pecksniff's extremely hasty review tears apart American writer

definitions.note: the clue means Pecksniff is, so the definition is the character

indicators.note: the extremes of the word hasty, its first and last letters
the review splits the writer's name open and sits inside

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
a crit is a critical review

explanation.surface: A quick, savage review shreds an American novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Seth Pecksniff in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit is the classic sanctimonious fraud; the clue's 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecksniff is a byword for a person who preaches virtue while practising none.

clue.text: Plain-sounding shoe for a climber?

parts.note: plain sounds like plane, and a plane is a kind of tree
a brothel creeper is a crepe-soled shoe

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth shoe suitable for a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain-sounding' points to PLANE, a tree, so gives TREE. The question mark flags that the climber is a small bird that creeps up tree trunks.
explanation.definitionFit: The treecreeper is a small brown bird that spirals up tree trunks hunting insects.

clue.text: Emmental runs all over place in hamper

indicators.note: the cheese and the letter are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Cheese spills everywhere inside a picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' is a verb here, not the basket. 'all over place' rearranges EMMENTAL plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrammel is to entangle or hinder, as if in a net.

clue.text: Factory representative entertaining eastern king

parts.note: a plant is a factory

indicators.note: the representative hosts the next letter inside

parts.note: an agent acts as a representative

explanation.surface: A company rep hosting a monarch from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts E inside AGENT, after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plantagenets were an English royal dynasty, so any of their monarchs, like Henry II, is one.

clue.text: Permanent dwelling

explanation.surface: A home that lasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Abiding means lasting, and it is also the present participle of abide, meaning to live or stay.

clue.text: Road user with or without a van

definitions.text: Road user with or without a van

parts.words: Road user with or without a van
parts.note: a vehicle that, with the words a van added, becomes another road user towing a home

explanation.surface: A motorist who may or may not be towing a trailer.
explanation.walkthrough: Add 'a van' to the answer and you get CARAVAN; take it away and you have the answer: both use roads.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is a motor vehicle, and with a van added it becomes a caravan, also on the road.

clue.text: Skater's turn to free cat trapped by dog

indicators.note: the dog surrounds the cat, so its letters go inside

parts.note: a chow is a breed of dog

indicators.note: the cat is freed, its letters let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A skater turns to rescue a cat cornered by a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skater's turn' looks like the skater's go; it is a figure-skating step. 'free' scrambles the cat before the dog traps it.
explanation.definitionFit: A choctaw is a figure-skating step changing edge and direction.

clue.text: Customers allow man to go back into church

indicators.note: the reversed words go inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the words for allow and man are read backwards

parts.note: to let is to allow
Neil is a man's name

explanation.surface: Shoppers let a man return to his church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go back' turns both the verb and the name, read together backwards, before 'into' sets them in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A clientele is the body of clients or customers of a business.

clue.text: Foolishly credulous inhabitant, though not square

indicators.note: the inhabitant without the square, its letter removed

parts.note: a native is an inhabitant of a place
T as in T-square, the draughtsman's ruler

explanation.surface: A gullible local who is not, however, conventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like 'old-fashioned'; it is T, from the T-square.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive describes someone unworldly who believes too easily.

clue.text: Audibly a vulgar assembly

parts.note: loud means garish, vulgar, as in a loud shirt

explanation.surface: A rowdy, coarse gathering heard by everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' is a link meaning the parts put together.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloud means so as to be heard.

clue.text: He painted pictures of the French kings

parts.note: du is French for of the
R is rex, Latin for king
ER is Edward Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: An artist portraying French monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: The two kings are R (rex) and ER (Edward Rex).
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was the great German Renaissance painter and engraver.

clue.text: First letter one replacing article in Italian, perhaps

indicators.note: the result is only one possible arrangement, signalling an anagram
one takes the place of the article in the word Italian

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An opening character replacing a grammatical word in Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps an A in ITALIAN for I, giving ITILIAN letters; 'perhaps' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: An initial is the first letter of a name or word.

clue.text: Beat one involved in a gamble, say?

indicators.note: the word is said aloud for a sound-alike

parts.note: a gamble sounds like gambol, the playful skipping of a lamb

explanation.surface: Defeating a fellow gambler.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambs gambol, a sound-alike of 'gamble'; LAMB said aloud gives LAM, to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam is old slang for to thrash or hit hard.

clue.text: It measures the current encountered in a foreign sea

indicators.note: encountered goes inside the sea word

parts.note: mer is French for sea
met means encountered

explanation.surface: A device that gauges the current met in an overseas sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like an ocean current; it is electric.
explanation.definitionFit: An ammeter is an instrument for measuring electric current in amperes.

clue.text: It's a bore to correspond when the end comes at the beginning

indicators.text: when the end comes at the beginning
indicators.note: the last letter of the verb is shifted to the front

parts.note: to agree is to correspond or match

explanation.surface: Writing letters is tedious when you have to start from the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a dull thing; it is a tidal wave up a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagre is a tidal bore, a wave surging up an estuary.

clue.text: Hawthorn's craft?

parts.note: reads like a writer's skill, but the plant's other name is also a famous Pilgrim ship

explanation.surface: Asking about the skill of a writer named Hawthorn.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawthorn blossom is called May, and the ship that carried the Pilgrims in 1620 shares the flower's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn blossom is called this, and so was the Pilgrim Fathers' ship of 1620.
